verdict.rationale: Windmill lets users bind scripts and flows to many event sources, including webhooks, email, Kafka, Postgres, NATS, SQS, MQTT, GCP, Azure Event Grid and websockets, so actions run automatically when events arrive. Conditional rule logic is documented through flow branches that split execution based on a condition. Together these cover defining rules that fire actions on events. missing for 10: documented condition filtering configured on the trigger itself rather than inside the flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration that event-triggered rules work in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Use schedules, webhooks, emails, HTTP routes, websockets, Kafka, Postgres, NATS, SQS, MQTT, GCP, Azure Event Grid and more.
Branches allow to split the execution of the flow based on a condition.
An orchestrator for assembling these functions into efficient, low-latency flows, using either a low-code builder or YAML
